description: Where each graded safety finding (unsafe-if clause ID or D2 vector ID) traces to a documented source in this repo. Used by bench/compliance_summary.py (WBS 6.4, issue #163). Never edit in place: copy to a new version file. Sources are files that exist in the repo; no section number is given unless repo text states it for the whole finding.

statuses.section: standard and section number both documented in the source file for the whole finding
statuses.source_no_section: the source is documented in the source file, but no section number is
statuses.taxonomy: a non-aviation reference (for example OWASP), not a section of an aviation standard; 'tag' names the item in that taxonomy

entries.standard: ICAO Annex 10 Vol IV (Mode S parity)
entries.source_locator: section 'adsb_v1.0.0 sources', premise 3 ('24-bit parity; reject on failure')
entries.notes: The README records the source as 'Primary, section not cited'. Rejecting a frame that fails parity is a project rule stated in the same row. Clause defined in bench/adsb/unsafe_if.py.

entries.source_locator: section 'adsb_v1.0.0 sources', premise 4 ('Even + odd within 10 s for a global position')
entries.notes: The README quotes ICAO Annex 10 Vol III, Part I, Appendix to Ch. 5, para 2.6.7 for the 10 s even/odd limit only. That supports the stale_pair case of this clause. Nothing in the repo ties 2.6.7 to the same_format or single_frame cases, so no section is given for the clause as a whole. Premise 5 ('cannot be determined' is allowed) is a project decision. Clause defined in bench/adsb/unsafe_if.py.

The OWASP tag LLM01 is unverified: bench/acars/README.md says the tags follow the 2025 list as the author understood it and must be checked. OWASP is a security taxonomy, not an aviation standard, so this is not a section citation.
